chapters.title: Chapter 2: Government-Backed and Fixed Return Options

lessons.title: Public Provident Fund (PPF): The 15-Year Tax-Free Workhorse

children.text: PPF is boring on purpose. There is no NAV to track, no market crash to panic over, and no product manager trying to sell you an upgrade. It is a government-backed savings account that locks your money for 15 years and pays interest that is completely tax-free. For long-term goals, that combination is hard to beat on a post-tax basis, as long as you understand exactly how the lock-in and interest calculation work.

markDefs.definition: Exempt-Exempt-Exempt: the contribution is deductible, the returns earned each year are tax-free, and the final withdrawal is tax-free.

children.text: Tax on any investment can hit at three points: when you put money in, while it grows, and when you take it out. PPF escapes all three, which makes it
. Your deposit qualifies under Section 123 (80C) on the old regime, the annual interest is exempt, and the maturity amount is exempt.

body.text: Only the entry benefit depends on your regime. Even if you are on the default new regime and get no 80C deduction, PPF interest and maturity stay tax-free. That keeps PPF relevant for new-regime taxpayers too.

body.title: Quick Check
body.textWithBlank: Because PPF deposits are deductible, its interest is tax-free and its maturity is tax-free, PPF is described as ___.
body.explanation: EEE stands for Exempt-Exempt-Exempt. On the new regime the first E falls away because there is no 80C deduction, but the second and third still apply.

children.text: What 15 Years of Maximum Deposits Grows Into

Assume you deposit ₹1,50,000 at the start of each financial year for 15 years and the rate stays at 7.1%. Because interest is credited once a year, the maturity value follows the future value of an annuity due.

body.label: The tax-free advantage over 15 years
body.context: The extra corpus PPF builds over a similar-rate FD, purely because its interest is never taxed. This is before counting the ₹46,800 a year in 80C savings for an old-regime taxpayer in the 30% slab.

body.text: The 7.1% is not guaranteed for 15 years. The Finance Ministry resets small savings rates every quarter. PPF has been at 7.1% since April 2020, but it was 8.7% in 2013-14 and 7.6% for much of 2018. The capital is safe; the rate is not fixed. Treat the projections above as illustrations, not promises.

children.text: PPF interest is calculated each month on the lowest balance between the close of the 5th day and the end of the month, and credited at the end of the financial year. A deposit made on the 6th earns nothing for that month. If you invest a lump sum, do it between 1 and 5 April to earn interest for all 12 months.

body.title: Timing Check
body.question: Kavya, an architect in Kolkata, deposits ₹1,50,000 in her PPF account on 6 April instead of 4 April. Roughly how much interest does she give up for April on this deposit, at 7.1%?
options: Nothing, because interest is credited only at year end
body.explanation: The deposit misses April's lowest-balance window, so it earns interest for 11 months instead of 12. One month's interest is ₹1,50,000 × 7.1% ÷ 12 = ₹887.50. Small in one year, but repeated over 15 years and compounded, the habit of depositing late costs real money.

children.text: The 15 years are counted from the end of the financial year in which you open the account, so the real tenure is 15 years plus part of a year. You are not completely stuck during that time. Here is the lifecycle of an account opened on 10 January 2019.

body.title: Life of a PPF account opened on 10 January 2019

events.title: Account opened
events.description: This counts as year 1, even though only about 3 months remain in the financial year.

events.title: Loan window
events.description: You can borrow up to 25% of the balance at the end of the second financial year before the year you apply, at 1% above the PPF rate.

events.title: Partial withdrawals allowed
events.description: One withdrawal a year, up to 50% of the lower of the balance at the end of the 4th preceding year or the end of the preceding year. Premature closure is also allowed for specified reasons.

events.title: Maturity
events.description: 15 full financial years after 31 March 2019. The entire balance can be withdrawn tax-free.

events.title: Extension decision
events.description: Apply within one year of maturity to extend in 5-year blocks with fresh deposits. Without applying, the account continues earning interest but without new deposits.

body.title: Your Turn: The Partial Withdrawal Limit
body.prompt: Sameer opened his PPF account in FY 2019-20 and wants to withdraw in FY 2026-27. His balance was ₹4,20,000 at the end of FY 2022-23 and ₹9,10,000 at the end of FY 2025-26. What is the maximum he can withdraw this year?
body.explanation: Counting back from FY 2026-27, the 4th preceding year is FY 2022-23 (₹4,20,000) and the preceding year is FY 2025-26 (₹9,10,000). The limit is 50% of the lower figure: 50% × ₹4,20,000 = ₹2,10,000. The rule deliberately uses the older, smaller balance so you cannot drain the account quickly.

Any post office or authorised bank such as SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank or Axis Bank. Most banks allow opening and deposits through net banking.
The account becomes discontinued. Revive it by paying ₹500 for each missed year plus a ₹50 penalty per year.
Allowed after 5 years from the end of the year of opening, only for serious illness, higher education or a change in residency status. Interest is cut by 1% from the date of opening.
Happens by default after maturity. Balance keeps earning interest, and you can withdraw any amount once a year.
Requires an application within one year of maturity. Withdrawals are capped at 60% of the balance at the start of each 5-year block.
In multiples of ₹50, as many times as you like in a year, as long as the yearly total stays between ₹500 and ₹1,50,000.

body.title: Scenario: PPF on the New Regime
body.scenario: Imran, 32, is a data analyst in Lucknow earning ₹20,00,000 a year. He is on the new regime, so his taxable income after the ₹75,000 standard deduction is ₹19,25,000, putting his top slab at 20%. He gets no 80C benefit. He already invests ₹25,000 a month in equity mutual funds for retirement and wants a safe, long-term component for his daughter's higher education in about 16 years. A friend says 'PPF is pointless on the new regime'.
body.prompt: Is his friend right? Make the case for or against PPF for Imran.
body.modelAnswer: His friend is wrong. Imran loses only the entry deduction. PPF interest and maturity remain tax-free on the new regime. At his 20% slab (20.8% with cess), a taxable instrument would need to yield about 7.1% ÷ (1 − 0.208) = 8.96% to match PPF's 7.1% post-tax. Few safe debt options offer that. His goal is about 16 years away, which fits the 15-year tenure plus part-year well, and PPF gives him a government-backed, non-market-linked balance to sit alongside his equity SIPs. The trade-offs to be clear about: the rate can be reset quarterly, withdrawals are restricted until year 7, and he should deposit before 5 April each year to get full interest. A reasonable plan is to use PPF for the safe portion of the education goal and keep equity funds for growth.

body.title: Go Deeper: The Real Cost of a PPF Deposit on the Old Regime

children.text: For an old-regime taxpayer whose full ₹1,50,000 deduction falls in the 30% slab, each deposit saves ₹46,800 in tax. The money that actually leaves their pocket is ₹1,03,200, yet the full ₹1,50,000 compounds tax-free inside the account.

content.caption: This is why PPF's effective return is higher than 7.1% for an old-regime taxpayer, but only if the 80C limit was not already full from EPF, insurance or tuition fees.

body.title: Running Your PPF Account Well
steps: Check whether you already have a PPF account, including an old one opened by a parent that may be discontinued
Link it to net banking so deposits take two minutes
Deposit your yearly amount between 1 and 5 April, or set a standing instruction for the 1st to 5th of each month
Deposit at least ₹500 every year so the account never lapses
Download the yearly statement and save it with your 80C proofs
Mark your maturity date in your calendar and decide on extension at least a year in advance

points: PPF is EEE: deposits qualify under Section 123 (80C) on the old regime, and interest and maturity are tax-free under both regimes.
The rate is 7.1% for July to September 2026, reset quarterly by the government and unchanged since April 2020.
₹1.5 lakh a year for 15 years at 7.1% grows to about ₹40.68 lakh, roughly ₹7.22 lakh more than a 7% FD for a 30% slab taxpayer.
Deposit between 1 and 5 April (or the 1st to 5th of each month) to earn full interest.
The account matures 15 full financial years after the year of opening, with loans from year 3 and partial withdrawals from year 7.
Losing the 80C deduction on the new regime does not make PPF pointless; the tax-free interest still matters.

body.text: This lesson is for educational purposes only and is not tax, legal or investment advice. PPF interest rates are reset quarterly and scheme rules can be amended by the government. Projections assume a constant rate and are illustrative. Consult a qualified professional for decisions specific to your situation.
